name: Intermittent fasting
intro: Where the timer and fasting phases are honest, and where an aggressive paywall waits.

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting Tracker:
apps.verdict: A clean intermittent fasting timer with no clutter. Install it, open it, and the countdown starts immediately, surfacing in Dynamic Island and on the lock screen.
apps.loved: The app lives in Dynamic Island and on the lock screen, giving you fasting status at a glance without unlocking your phone. Users consistently call this system-level integration the app's biggest win.
apps.weak: No way to edit a timer once it's started or after it ends, so a misclick means a lost record. No sync between iPhone and iPad, so your data only exists on one device.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants a single-purpose tool with no extras: tap once, the timer runs, the number is always visible in Dynamic Island.

quotes.text: I really hate that I can't edit the time I started fasting I can only start the fast in real time. All of my times are off because of it.

Many applications that I tried complicate things and starts the apps with unnecessary questions to end up giving you multiple paid suggestions!! This app is to the point, download ➡️ open ➡️ start the timer!! It also has a widget, and also it appears on lock screen..

Many applications that I tried complicate things and starts the apps with unnecessary questions to end up giving you multiple paid suggestions!! This app is to the point, download ➡️ open ➡️ start the timer!!

apps.title: Easy Fast Tracker: FastMinder
apps.verdict: The best value-for-reliability pick in the category. Includes a Watch app, a Mac app with iCloud sync, Live Activities, widgets, and educational fasting stages. A go-to choice for users who left the Life app. The paid barrier at install hurts conversion.
apps.loved: Mac plus iOS sync over iCloud is unique in this category. Educational content explaining what your body is doing at each fasting stage. A first-class Watch app with detailed on-screen info.
apps.weak: A paywall hits users on the main screen before they can try anything. The custom notification takes up too much space and is not configurable. Problems entering a future fast start time (the date resets).
apps.whoFor: Experienced IF practitioners who are invested in the Apple ecosystem (Watch, Mac, iPhone) and already know why they need a tracker. Works well for people running varied protocols including extended fasts.

apps.title: Fasting Tracker • Easy Fast
apps.verdict: The cleanest timer in the category. Shows the current metabolic phase (gluconeogenesis, fat burning, ketosis) right on the dial, which genuinely helps you push through. The free version is functional, paid adds programs and extra stats. Main downside: no sync between iPhone and iPad.
apps.loved: A live fasting-phase display tied to elapsed hours. Users say this is exactly what keeps them inside their fasting window until the end.
apps.weak: No automatic schedule repeat: you have to manually start a new fast every day.
apps.whoFor: Any IF practitioner from beginner to advanced who wants clear visual phase feedback without extra screens.

quotes.text: Used this app quite a bit to log my fasts… just updated and lost it all…. Have to jump through hoops (after update) only to land on a page that is $9.99 /mo or 49.99 /year.
I love that the app includes what stage of fasting you're in per hour: Gluconeogenesis, Fat Burning and Ketosis. It's so helpful and helps me stay in my fast. And this is just the free version!

I was able to install this on ipad, iphone, and apple watch. But i cannot figure out how to sync between devices. I have to start and end each fast in each device. That limits its usefulness a lot. Please let me know if there is some setting I need to change. Otherwise, I'll need to stick to Zero wh

apps.title: Daily Fast
apps.verdict: Daily Fast is a rare minimalist tracker with no subscriptions and no attempt to bloat the feature set. Users come back to it after trying more complex apps. Main weaknesses: notifications can miss and there is no widget.
apps.loved: A built-in schedule means you never have to manually start or stop. The app knows when you are fasting. Zero monetization pressure and no lifestyle questions on launch.
apps.weak: Notifications about the approaching eating window are unreliable. You cannot edit past-day times. Does not support fasts longer than 24 hours.
apps.whoFor: An experienced 16:8 practitioner who wants a quiet, accurate timer with no upselling and no subscription.

quotes.text: Best fasting app I've found so far. No subscription, gimmicky groups or unnecessary features. I'd add a fifth star if it had a widget so I would quickly see my time without opening the app.
I enjoy everything about this app, except that there is no audible alert to notify eating window, and fasting start time. It would be nice to hear an alert when I am busy elsewhere.

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting Tracker ⁺
apps.verdict: A gamified tracker where a virtual garden grows with your fasting hours. Also tracks water, menstrual cycle, and mood. A lock screen widget with a countdown is one of its key features. A lifetime purchase option lowers the barrier.
apps.loved: The growing virtual garden mechanic creates an engagement loop. Users say they do not want to kill their plant. Toggleable modules let you keep only the trackers you need without a cluttered home screen.
apps.weak: Custom fast durations outside of presets require a paid upgrade. There is no way to transfer data between iOS and Android, so your history and garden are gone if you switch platforms. Widgets show only the timer, not the garden.
apps.whoFor: People who need game-like motivation to build a fasting habit, especially a younger audience.

quotes.text: I really hate that I can't edit the time I started fasting I can only start the fast in real time. All of my times are off because of it.

Many applications that I tried complicate things and starts the apps with unnecessary questions to end up giving you multiple paid suggestions!! This app is to the point, download ➡️ open ➡️ start the timer!! It also has a widget, and also it appears on lock screen..

Many applications that I tried complicate things and starts the apps with unnecessary questions to end up giving you multiple paid suggestions!! This app is to the point, download ➡️ open ➡️ start the timer!!

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting Timer
apps.verdict: A minimalist timer with no subscriptions. Does one thing honestly. Main flaw: stats are calculated incorrectly. The 7-day average includes all data from the beginning of use, not a rolling week. Weight entries have no year, so data from multiple years gets mixed together.
apps.loved: One start/stop button, an Apple Watch widget, no pushy notifications, and no paid pressure. You can also backdate the start time of a fast.
apps.weak: Statistics use a running total instead of a sliding window, making them misleading. Weight log entries show no year, so multi-year data becomes unreadable. Cannot log more than one fast per day.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants to tap a button and stop thinking. No education, no progress charts, just a clean timer with a weight log.

apps.title: Cronometer: Calorie Counter
apps.verdict: The most nutritionally detailed free food tracker available, covering micronutrients alongside macros and including a web version. Loosely connected to fasting as a practice.
apps.loved: The only free tracker that breaks down not just macros but micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) with per-meal detail. The barcode scanner recognizes almost everything without a miss.
apps.weak: After a recent update, search surfaces branded products above generic names, turning a simple query like 'banana' into a multi-step hunt. This breaks the core fast-logging use case.
apps.whoFor: People who want full control over their diet with a focus on nutrients rather than just calories, and who are not looking for a dedicated fasting timer.

apps.title: Sunrise - Intermittent Fasting
apps.verdict: A minimalist free tracker with no subscription pressure. Core feature: a clean timer with manual start and end entry, a monthly calendar view, and basic weight tracking. Breaks after some updates, with the widget failing to reset and sessions not saving on exit.
apps.loved: The ability to log a past fast retroactively and see a color-coded tile for the entire month keeps the feeling of a streak going.
apps.weak: No daily reminders on a set schedule. Users have to remember to start the timer themselves.
apps.whoFor: An experienced 16:8 or 18:6 practitioner who wants an honest archive without a subscription or extra screens.

quotes.text: I want an app that remind me every day, not an app that I have to remind every day.

I only wish it had a count down for the feeding window as well, not just the fast portion. Other than that, simple, straight forward, perfect. The ability to edit the start and finish time of the fast is a great and obvious feature that other IF apps didn't have.

apps.title: Suavita: Fasting Tracker App
apps.verdict: Suavita stands out for supporting extended fasts beyond 7 days, a niche competitors do not cover. Hourly milestones explain what is happening in your body. Weak points: limited record editing and typos in the copy.
apps.loved: Support for 40-plus-day extended fasts with hourly physiological cues. The visual progress ring and pie chart keep you motivated to continue.
apps.weak: Cannot edit or delete a fast once it has started. The time-picker scroll is finicky. A recent update removed some free features without notice.
apps.whoFor: Extended fasting practitioners (24-plus hours) who want a tracker with physiological context.

apps.title: BodyOK: Intermittent Fasting
apps.verdict: One of the more mature trackers in the category: auto-detects fasting patterns, offers presets with notifications, and lets you delete a failed fast from history. Stability drops after major updates, but the team actively patches issues.
apps.loved: Automatic fasting pattern presets with push notifications for the start and end of a fast take the guesswork out of your schedule. The ability to delete a fast from history without penalty helps you keep accurate stats.
apps.weak: After updates the app sometimes fails to register that a fast ended and shows 'Start' instead of 'End', causing data loss. Apple Health weight sync does not work consistently.
apps.whoFor: People who want a simple, reliable timer with notifications and have no interest in food or meal plans.

quotes.text: This helps a lot for me to stick to fasting. I guess seeing it count makes it easier. The only reason I didn't give it a 5 star was because you input your weight. And you can have it sync to you health data from apple but it doesn't actually sync. So your weight doesn't get updated in this app.

apps.title: Senza: Keto & Fasting
apps.verdict: The best free keto tracker with a fasting window bundled in, but intermittent journal load failures undermine reliability.
apps.loved: Automatically calculates net carbs and builds keto-oriented recipes, removing the main pain point for keto beginners.
apps.weak: The journal periodically stops loading for days at a time, and the support page returns a 404, leaving users without any help.
apps.whoFor: People combining a ketogenic diet with intermittent fasting who want one tool for both.

quotes.text: I love this app, it's helped me lose 20lbs in a month. The one thing that I find so incredibly frustrating is that you cannot go backwards and see the values previously entered on data points on the weight chart. I don't know why this wouldn't be an available function, it just doesn't make sense.

apps.title: Fasting Tracker App - Fasta
apps.verdict: A minimalist tracker focused purely on fasting time with no extra features. The editable fast history is genuinely appreciated by disciplined trackers. Apple Watch runs as a fully independent app with no phone sync.
apps.loved: Editable fast history lets you fix an incorrect start or stop without losing your data. Metabolic state display (ketosis, stable glucose) based on elapsed fasting time, no lab work required.
apps.weak: Apple Watch and iPhone run completely independently, giving you two unsynced counters at the same time. The streak counter breaks for fasts longer than 25 hours, counting them as skipped days. No countdown timer to the end of the eating window.
apps.whoFor: People who want a clean minimalist fast log with no keto advice and no gamification.

apps.title: Fasting Secret
apps.verdict: A minimalist tracker focused on visualizing the current fast and showing a calendar history. The paid retroactive-start feature (manually setting a past fast's start time) is genuinely useful for regular practitioners. The 48-hour fast cap cuts off extended fasting.
apps.loved: A real-time visual countdown keeps the current fast front of mind. The retroactive-start feature lets you log a fast honestly even if you forgot to tap the button on time.
apps.weak: Maximum fast length of 48 hours is not enough for extended formats. No Apple Health or Apple Watch integration despite repeated user requests. The weight goal feature is inaccessible after purchasing premium.
apps.whoFor: People doing 16:8 or 18:6 who want a simple tracker with a history and no extra features.

quotes.text: A great app for manually tracking weight and fasts. The one huge downside for me is that there is no way to set a target fasting duration without an exact time, ex: target 18 hours, not 5pm to 11am. I don't know anyone who manages to start and end their fasts at the exact same minute each day.

apps.title: FastHabit Intermittent Fasting
apps.verdict: A minimalist fasting timer that degraded after monetization. Features that used to be free are now locked behind a subscription.
apps.loved: Users value the clean interface and the ability to control the timer directly from Apple Watch.
apps.weak: Data does not transfer when switching phones, the widget does not work, and support is unresponsive. These are critical failures for long-term habit tracking.
apps.whoFor: Apple Watch users who want to start and stop a fast with a flick of the wrist.

quotes.text: iPhone widget doesn't work. Just a blur of letters and numbers. No widget at all for the phone. If you open the app the timer works but that's about all it's good for. Much better apps out there.

I had enjoyed the FastHabit app, but I got a new phone today, and all of my data is now missing. And this is despite the fact that I pay for the premium version and had all of my data saved to my phones cloud. There is also no way to contact any sort of customer support.

Hi, I have been using the app (paid version) for few months now, just want to report an issue with the App UI and sync with Apple Watch Ultra. The tracker on watch goes out of sync and does not reflect the values displayed on the iPhone app.
Push notifications work half the time, bought new phone and all recorded fasts were gone forever, not retrievable.

I love the simplicity of this app and that I can start and stop my timer on my Apple Watch. But there is one thing missing that would make it 5 stars. Please consider showing the eating window times in addition to the fasting window. Many fasters, myself included, now focus on the feast window.

apps.title: Fast: Intermittent Fasting App
apps.verdict: Fast uses an educational timer that shows fasting phases (blood sugar drop, fat-burning zone, ketosis) in real time. A buddy system adds social motivation. Analytics are buggy, fast start times cannot be edited retroactively, and the app occasionally crashes.
apps.loved: A live timer with named metabolic phases keeps users aware of exactly what is happening right now. Buddy fasting with real-time status of friends adds accountability.
apps.weak: The fast history adds ghost entries and shows incorrect hours on the All tab. You cannot change the start time of a completed fast. Achievements do not save.
apps.whoFor: People who find it easier to stay on track with a group and want to understand what is happening in their body hour by hour.

quotes.text: I've tried every fasting app and always come back to this one. My favorite feature is the timer that also educational. It helps awareness of your internal process like when you are lowering your blood sugar, in the fat burning zone, the ketosis zone. It is extremely motivational!

apps.title: Rhythm: Fasting Tracker
apps.verdict: A beautiful minimalist timer that users appreciate for its honesty (no subscriptions). Known limitations have been present for years: 24-hour cap, the timer auto-stops at the goal, no multiple fasts per day, no retroactive time entry. The most recent major update broke the history.
apps.loved: No paywalls. A visually clean interface with a fork-and-clock design. Six years of operation without core feature degradation, up until the most recent update.
apps.weak: A hard 24-hour cap is a dealbreaker for OMAD or multi-day fasting. The timer stops when the goal is reached instead of continuing to count. A rolling 7-day history means older fasts fall off the widget. Start-of-fast notifications do not fire.
apps.whoFor: People practicing standard 16:8 or 18:6 with no need for extended fasts, who value simplicity and a subscription-free experience.

apps.title: Fastic Weight Loss & Fasting
apps.verdict: A fasting tracker with a nice widget and a community feature, but overloaded with ads to the point that even paid users complain.
apps.loved: The lock screen widget and the header timer gave users an instant summary without opening the app. Users directly name this as the main hook that kept them coming back.
apps.weak: The team moved the timer off the main screen into a buried navigation layer, breaking the primary UX pattern for loyal users. Switching to a new phone does not restore the account, so all progress is lost.
apps.whoFor: Beginners who want a polished interface and reminders, and who are willing to tolerate ads or pay for Plus upfront.

quotes.text: When I upgraded my phone, the app wouldn't recognize me and I had to start over. I get a random 'you've completed your first fast' about once a month. Every frosty is my first frosty. Deleted alerts keep reappearing. Kinda lame.

apps.title: KetoDiet: Fasting & Meal Plans
apps.verdict: A keto tracker focused on recipes and meal planning. The food database and barcode scanner work, but macros are often inaccurate and need manual checking. The scanner misidentifies products. The interface feels overwhelming for new users.
apps.loved: A recipe planner with macro counts gives users a structured weekly eating plan. Mood and energy tracking alongside food logs is a rare feature that helps reveal patterns.
apps.weak: The barcode scanner maps products incorrectly, such as identifying cheese as a sandwich. Minimum vegetable portions are locked at one cup with no way to reduce. The food database is geared toward European products, with many American entries missing.
apps.whoFor: People strictly tracking keto macros who want to cook from recipes rather than just fast by the clock.

apps.title: Litely-Food Tracker & Wellness
apps.verdict: A fasting tracker plus food journal with AI recognition and recipes. The interface gets praise for visual clarity. Two systemic failures hurt trust: a forced subscription screen with no close button blocks the app, and logging out wipes fasting history with no way to recover it.
apps.loved: The visual daily fasting progress combined with themed recipes creates a sense of being guided rather than just tracked.
apps.weak: A forced paywall with no option to dismiss makes the app unusable for some users.
apps.whoFor: Users ready to pay from day one who want to combine IF with meal tracking.

apps.title: IF: Intermittent Fasting 16:8
apps.verdict: IF 16:8 stands out with an onboarding education section for beginners and avatars representing diverse racial backgrounds, which is unusual for the genre. The timer works and reminders arrive. However, daylight saving time shifts break the schedule, weight conversion is unreliable, and support is silent.
apps.loved: An educational section covering IF basics is available without a subscription and helps beginners get started. Automatic reminders for the start and end of a fast require no manual tap.
apps.weak: When clocks change for daylight saving, the timer goes off and there is no manual correction. Weight conversion to pounds does not work. The paid content behind the subscription, five recipes, is a disappointment.
apps.whoFor: Beginners who want a basic explanation of intermittent fasting and automatic reminders.

apps.title: Fasting For Weight Loss App
apps.verdict: An all-in-one tool combining a fasting timer, step counter, water tracker, and AI food recognition. The coaching feature works, but the coach responds with a 4-5 hour delay. The food database is unreliable: the barcode scanner assigns portion sizes arbitrarily, and coffee is measured in grams instead of milliliters.
apps.loved: AI photo food recognition lowers the barrier for logging meals. A photo of your plate is enough.
apps.weak: The food database returns incorrect weights and units, and calorie counts do not match real-world food.
apps.whoFor: Beginners who want a single dashboard without diving deep into nutrition science.

quotes.text: I typically do 19/5, but it's not an option in the app, so I have to do 18/6 and let it go an extra hour. It would be very helpful if you put in all the possibilities including 19/5, 21/3, 22/2.

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting: PureFast
apps.verdict: A fitness tracker with workouts and a fasting timer, but the reliability of both components raises questions.
apps.loved: A wide variety of workouts at different intensity levels resonates with users who combine IF with physical activity.
apps.weak: The timer stops when you close the app. After paying for a workout plan, the app begins showing every day as a rest day.
apps.whoFor: People who want to combine fasting tracking and home workouts in a single app.

apps.title: BodyFast: Intermittent Fasting
apps.verdict: A fasting tracker with a weekly schedule from a 'coach' that suggests different fasting protocols suited to your personal rhythm.
apps.loved: A weekly auto-scheduled plan with protocol suggestions (16:8, 5:2, and others) reduces decision fatigue. You do not need to figure out today's protocol on your own.
apps.weak: The schedule cannot be copied to the next week, so you reconfigure from scratch every time. On top of that, the schedule editor's own logic (times cannot overlap mid-edit) makes the process take far longer than it should.
apps.whoFor: People who want a structured fasting plan with varied protocols and prefer not to design their own schedule.

quotes.text: Everything is fine except for creating your schedule. There's no option of using the same schedule you set prior. So, you have to edit it every week. Along with doing that, it takes so long to edit it because no times can overlap WHILE editing in order for them NOT to overlap, which makes it harder.

apps.title: Fasting + Intermittent Fasting
apps.verdict: A timer with a phase display and a built-in meal planner. Key product flaw: in the free version, ads cover the button to end a fast, so users physically cannot save their result. The coaching feature exists, but dietary tips do not adapt to your chosen diet (a keto plan gets low-calorie recommendations).
apps.loved: The phase display and motivational push notifications at key milestones (18h, 24h) help users resist quitting.
apps.weak: In the free version, ads block the fast-ending button, which breaks the core mechanic of the tracker.
apps.whoFor: Paid subscribers who want a combined timer and meal planner and are not concerned about nutrient accuracy.

quotes.text: The app uses different phsicologic tools to make fasting easier. I can easy to for 18 hours without too much struggle as each phase motivates me to push even more.

apps.title: Feel Great - Fasting Coach
apps.verdict: A Unicity-backed tracker with educational videos from physicians and support for night-shift schedules. Data disappears in certain in-app navigation scenarios, destroying months of history. The educational content for beginners is strong.
apps.loved: An educational section with videos from doctors and specialists gives beginners context on why to fast and what happens in the body. Dedicated buttons for Unimate and Balance products are convenient for users in the Unicity ecosystem.
apps.weak: Navigating to the in-app store section resets all data, a systemic bug that destroys trust. The app does not adapt to night-shift workers: the eating window cannot flex to non-standard schedules.
apps.whoFor: Unicity product users and people just starting out with fasting who want to understand the mechanics.

quotes.text: I was loving the app and logging my data, until I lost it all after 60+ days of tracking and couldn't retrieve it. I was trying to refer Unicity to a friend, and the app was requiring me to logon even though I was already logged in, so I did and at that point I lost everything.
I don't like that you reset the fasting goal if you don't log each day. I left my phone at home and didn't log my goal until the next day and I lost my streak.

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting Tracker -
apps.verdict: A basic tracker that gradually degraded due to growing ad load and an unstable timer.
apps.loved: The app provides fasting phase context and responds to user progress, which creates a sense of support.
apps.weak: The timer resets or freezes when you leave the app, and the screen fills with food ads in the middle of a fast, which defeats the entire point of tracking.
apps.whoFor: IF beginners who have not yet discovered better alternatives.

quotes.text: I really hate that I can't edit the time I started fasting I can only start the fast in real time. All of my times are off because of it.

Many applications that I tried complicate things and starts the apps with unnecessary questions to end up giving you multiple paid suggestions!! This app is to the point, download ➡️ open ➡️ start the timer!! It also has a widget, and also it appears on lock screen..

Many applications that I tried complicate things and starts the apps with unnecessary questions to end up giving you multiple paid suggestions!! This app is to the point, download ➡️ open ➡️ start the timer!!

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting - MyFast
apps.verdict: MyFast offered a simple schedule with no bloat, and for a long time that was its strength. The app has not been updated in years (the website dates to 2014), data gets lost, and push notifications arrive at random times. Users are leaving.
apps.loved: Schedule mode automatically tracks eating windows without manual start/stop taps. A configurable schedule with daily reminders works for people with a stable routine.
apps.weak: Data disappears without warning. In schedule mode there is no way to manually log when you actually started or stopped fasting. Notifications arrive at random times.
apps.whoFor: A user with a fixed 16:8 schedule who does not need history and just wants a reminder.

apps.title: AI Calorie Tracker by Yazio
apps.verdict: A food tracker with AI portion analysis and a polished interface that degraded due to unskippable educational animations after every meal log.
apps.loved: AI food photo analysis with portion estimates works surprisingly well. Users note it lowers the effort of logging complex dishes that are hard to find in the database.
apps.weak: After every food entry, the app forces an animated tip that cannot be turned off anywhere in settings. This breaks the daily use rhythm and is directly cited as the main reason users delete the app.
apps.whoFor: Users who want AI dish photo analysis and a polished interface and can tolerate persistent educational content.

quotes.text: После обновления пропал параметр скинутого веса из измерений. Почему? Я с удовольствием наблюдала эту цифру. Верните, пожалуйста!

Overall, the app is great, but the Meal Tips need some work. They always seem to find something to criticize, even when the meal is perfectly fine. For example, I logged Konjac Rice (20 calories per 200g), and the tip suggested replacing it with a lower-calorie alternative. Seriously?

Бош буквально на второй день при добавлении блюда КАЖДЫЙ РАЗ вы терроризируете СОВЕТАМИ от которых невозможно отказаться. После этого вы втираете мне платную подписку. Весь этот процесс отнимает МИНУТУ МОЕЙ ЖИЗНИ. Короче, удаляю.

apps.title: Kompanion: Weight Loss Plan
apps.verdict: Combines a fasting timer, calorie counter, and phase display in a single interface. The food scanner is unreliable, with some products recognized only through manual entry. Key product downside: the metabolic phase display (from glycolysis to ketosis) requires a subscription.
apps.loved: A real-time fasting phase display visually motivates users to hold out until ketosis.
apps.weak: The food scanner frequently fails to identify a product and returns zero calories, making nutrition data unreliable.
apps.whoFor: Users combining intermittent fasting with calorie counting who can tolerate an imperfect food tracker.

apps.title: Zero: Fasting & Food Tracker
apps.verdict: An intermittent fasting timer with a polished fat-burning phase visualization, but the free version's functionality is cut to a bare minimum.
apps.loved: A 'flame' animation during peak fat-burning phase genuinely motivates users to keep going. People who lost 20-30 pounds credit this visual cue as a key driver.
apps.weak: The target weight algorithm has a serious bug: it substitutes someone else's parameters in place of the ones you entered. The app gives no warning about maximum safe fasting duration, which is a risk for vulnerable users.
apps.whoFor: People willing to pay for a subscription from day one who want motivating phase visualization.

quotes.text: The meal logger is so obnoxious. I could eat an entire buffalo and wheel of cheese and this stupid thing would still be like, 'yeah, maybe you should add an egg for extra protein next time.'

apps.title: Lose Weight at Home in 30 Days
apps.short: Lose Weight at Home in 30 Days
apps.verdict: A home fitness app with workouts, not a fasting tracker.
apps.loved: Users point to ready-made workout plans and on-screen instructions that are clear even for beginners.
apps.weak: No adaptation for physical limitations (knee, back issues). Jumping exercises are presented as the only option with no alternative.
apps.whoFor: People without injuries who are looking for structured home workouts.

apps.title: Fastin: Intermittent Fasting
apps.verdict: A fasting tracker with a reasonable feature set (timer, phases, hydration, food) but a broken logging mechanic: you cannot fix an incorrect start time, and the log freezes when you try to edit. The app auto-switches your plan if you deviate by even an hour, which irritates experienced users. Works more like a reminder than a precise tool.
apps.loved: Progress challenges and hydration reminders help people starting from scratch maintain their rhythm.
apps.weak: Editing entries freezes or is unavailable, and the plan automatically switches when the schedule slips even slightly.
apps.whoFor: A beginner who needs a simple push to get through the first month and does not care about log accuracy.

quotes.text: This is an easy and straight forward fasting timer app but I've had this for years and have never been able to go back and edit a fasting entry (if I made a mistake on the time or something) without the app freezing and shutting down… it would be nice if the app actually let you edit fasting logs.

apps.title: Fasting App: Tracker & Timer
apps.verdict: An aggressive onboarding flow with 25 to 30 questions leads straight to a paywall. Most angry reviews are about exactly that. The timer itself works, but data occasionally disappears. The product is dishonest with new users.
apps.loved: A visual fasting phase breakdown with body-state labels and progress notifications resonate with users who make it past the onboarding.
apps.weak: A 30-question onboarding with no product preview first creates a feeling of being misled. Fast history has disappeared without explanation. The interface does not fit newer iPhone screen sizes.
apps.whoFor: A beginner willing to sit through an aggressive sales flow in exchange for a polished phase timer.

quotes.text: When an app asked me 30 questions before I even get a chance to set it up I am suddenly see a huge paywall. I don't even know what this because I deleted it after about the 25th question some of them phrased like a goofy sales pitch. Moving on looking for something else now.

apps.title: Fasting Tracker & Diet App
apps.verdict: A bare-bones timer with no way to backdate start or end times. It works right up until the first time you forget to tap.
apps.loved: No subscriptions and no ads. Users appreciate that the app does one thing and does not get in the way.
apps.weak: No editing of start or end times. That is a fatal flaw for a tracker people run in the background rather than watch in real time.
apps.whoFor: People with very disciplined routines who always remember to tap the button on time.

quotes.text: I do appreciate that this is a simple and straightforward timing app and nothing more than you need. It's easy to use and I do appreciate the notifications. The only thing it is missing is the ability to change the start or end times. Sometimes I forget to start my fast time on the app or I'm not ne

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting Skip Meal
apps.verdict: The app promises a tracker but real users hit an aggressive paywall after two days, login failures after updates, and crashes during water logging. Functionally weak.
apps.loved: Fasting start and hydration reminders work for beginners. The interface is simple enough to not confuse new users in the first few days.
apps.weak: The timer is unstable and the app crashes when logging water. After updates, authentication breaks so users who paid can no longer get in. The subscription scheme pushes people away before they can evaluate the product.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone in its current state. If the app is fixed and the forced early paywall is removed, it could work for absolute IF beginners.

apps.title: DoFasting Intermittent Fasting
apps.verdict: DoFasting is positioned as a coaching platform, but the back button does not work on newer iPhones, canceling a subscription is made deliberately difficult, and support sends templated responses. Educational content exists but is blocked by technical problems.
apps.loved: A countdown widget to the end of the fast is actively used. A food diary with a product database helps beginners structure their eating.
apps.weak: Navigation is broken on iPhone 16/17 Pro Max: the back button is covered by the status bar. The subscription cancellation flow is deliberately obscured. It does not cancel through the App Store and requires a separate email.
apps.whoFor: A beginner looking for structure and recipes who can tolerate interface instability.

quotes.text: I'm new to fasting and have found the daily goals, meal ideas and fasting 'how to' resources valuable as I start my journey.

apps.title: FastEasy: Intermittent Fasting
apps.verdict: A minimalist fasting timer with fasting phase information, but with serious stability problems and questionable subscription practices.
apps.loved: In-context content about what happens in your body at hour 4, 8, and 16 helps beginners stay motivated without separate reading.
apps.weak: The app has no way to log food with a barcode or scan calories, forcing users to switch to another service for a full picture. The absence of a basic calorie counter makes it a halfway tool.
apps.whoFor: People just starting intermittent fasting who want a simple timer with motivating content and no extra features.

apps.title: Prime: Intermittent Fasting
apps.verdict: The app does not let you pause a fast without deleting your account entirely. The eating window does not update when you change settings. Notifications do not work. Articles in the education section repeat themselves. For the price, users feel cheated.
apps.loved: A live chat coach who answers questions about supplements and vitamins is the only feature users praise with specifics.
apps.weak: No way to pause a fast without resetting the entire account. The eating window does not save changes. Content in the education section is duplicated from article to article.
apps.whoFor: Someone for whom live coach access matters and timer precision does not.

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting Hero Diet
apps.verdict: A free tracker with a simple timer, but with serious stability problems. The app resets the date to an incorrect value, loses all history on logout, and prompts re-login every few days.
apps.loved: Simplicity: one screen with a timer and no extra settings, which works for complete fasting beginners.
apps.weak: The session resets every few days and wipes the entire fast history even when you sign back in with the same account. The bar chart shows scheduled time instead of actual fasting time.
apps.whoFor: People who want to try fasting without commitment and are okay with losing their history.

apps.title: WeFast: Diet Plan for Women
apps.verdict: A once-popular tracker with a female audience that has degraded to a non-functional state. After several updates the app does not load for a large share of users, Apple Sign-In is broken, and the community was moved to an external Facebook group. Those who do manage to open it praise the simple timer.
apps.loved: A simple visual progress bar and a fast history feed kept users engaged for years.
apps.weak: The app does not launch after updates: it freezes on the logo for one to several minutes and does not save sessions.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone in its current state. Historically it worked well for women new to 16:8 fasting.

apps.title: Unimeal: Fasting and Diet
apps.verdict: A diet plan with a fasting window, known to users primarily for a subscription scheme that is deliberately difficult to cancel.
apps.loved: Ready-made meal plans with recipes reduce cognitive load in the first days.
apps.weak: The food database is too sparse for self-directed logging. The fasting timer functions as a diary rather than an active tracking tool.
apps.whoFor: An audience that needs rigid external structure for eating and does not plan to keep a detailed food log.

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting for Men
apps.verdict: The app is marketed as a tracker for men, but the basic function of switching IF protocols is buried behind a paywall and is genuinely hard to find. The calorie counter only covers branded products. A spiritual mechanic that asks for religious affiliation feels out of place in a health tracker.
apps.loved: A progress page showing fasting days gives users a sense of accumulated results over several weeks.
apps.weak: Switching from 16:8 to 18:6 is buried deep in settings and often does not save. The calorie database covers only store brands with no way to add your own meal. The timer merges multiple days together rather than counting them individually.
apps.whoFor: Hard to name a clear audience. The product wins neither on simplicity nor on depth.

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting Tracker!
apps.verdict: A survey onboarding that leads directly to a subscription screen with no way to try the app first. Content contains grammar errors. There is virtually no real tracking in the free version.
apps.loved: The eating window structure and fast period reminders give users a sense of having a schedule.
apps.weak: No access to any features without a subscription, even after completing the survey. Interface typos reduce trust in the data.
apps.whoFor: Very hard to name an audience. The app does not let users try it before paying.

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting Tracker ™
apps.verdict: A fasting timer that cannot even edit start or end times. Data resets after a few days. The app is marketed as free but immediately pushes a payment screen.
apps.loved: One-tap timer launch with no setup. Users note you can start immediately.
apps.weak: No way to correct the end time of a past fast retroactively. If you forget to tap, the data is gone. The app periodically wipes the entire history without warning.

apps.title: Go Fasting－Weight Loss Tracker
apps.verdict: A minimal tracker with non-functional time editing, no fasting methodology content, and an opaque subscription cancellation flow. Does not support OMAD. Marketed as free but features are locked behind a paywall.
apps.loved: No mechanics worth highlighting. Users found no value beyond the basic timer.
apps.weak: Editing the fast start time causes a crash. No fasting methodology content at all. Water is measured only in liters with no way to switch to ounces.

apps.title: Intermittent Fasting and Diet.
apps.verdict: The app systematically fails to open for a large share of users (white screen on launch). Support has not responded to emails for months. Documented cases of unsubscribable subscriptions. As a fasting tracker it has a timer and fasting articles, but they are inaccessible if the app does not start.
apps.loved: The dashboard design and navigation are appreciated by the rare users for whom the app actually opens.
apps.weak: The app does not launch on a significant portion of devices, showing a white screen with no fallback and no support response.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone in its current state.

apps.title: Fasting Tracker App
apps.verdict: Effectively a timer that demands payment of around $44 per year from the first screen. Users report inability to cancel the subscription, unexpected charges, and no value beyond what a phone's built-in clock provides.
apps.loved: Nothing substantial. Some users mention simplicity, but this is the only app in the set with not a single honest positive observation about the product itself.
apps.weak: A forced annual subscription from the first screen with no way to evaluate the product first. Impossible to cancel through standard Apple interfaces. Static content with recipes that are never updated.
apps.whoFor: No one.
